name: Peeschute
tagline: Disposable unisex urine bags for travel and patient care
excerpt: Peeschute makes a disposable unisex urine bag and won a ₹75 lakh commitment from Aman Gupta on Shark Tank India Season 1.
content:
Peeschute makes a paper-based, disposable urine bag that anyone can use when no clean toilet is nearby, on long road trips or for elderly and bed-ridden patients. Founder Siddhant Tawarawala, who grew up in Jalna in Maharashtra, came up with it after long bus rides home and developed it with support from an Ahmedabad incubator.

On Shark Tank India's first season, boAt co-founder Aman Gupta made an investment commitment of ₹75 lakh. Gupta said the hygiene market in India needed products like this.

We could not find a filing-based report of Peeschute's revenue, funding or valuation since the show, so those are listed as not publicly disclosed.

faq.q: Did Peeschute get a deal on Shark Tank India?
faq.a: Aman Gupta made a ₹75 lakh investment commitment. The equity figure was not confirmed by an outlet we rely on.
Its website is live, but we found no recent filing-based report on the company.

lessons: Our analysis: a product that solves an awkward, everyday problem can stand out on TV precisely because people rarely talk about it.
